nodes.label: Explicit Confirmation Boundary
nodes.rationale: Keeping the preview in the browser until confirmation lets users review columns and catch mapping issues before backend validation and AI extraction begin.

nodes.label: Extra Contact Value Preservation
nodes.rationale: Extra contact values are appended to crm_note instead of being silently discarded.

nodes.label: Import Workbench
nodes.rationale: The interface is a quiet, evidence-first operational workbench so reviewers can inspect messy data without decorative UI competing for attention.

nodes.label: Evidence Color Rule
nodes.source_location: Design System: Listwright > Colors > Named Rules
nodes.rationale: Status color must always be paired with text, an icon, or a shape so meaning never depends on color alone.

nodes.label: Auditable Import Workflow
nodes.rationale: AI output is constrained and backend-normalized so a reviewer can trace what changed instead of treating the model as authority.

nodes.label: Reviewer-Fast Demo
nodes.rationale: A sample CSV should demonstrate the complete workflow in one sitting without accounts, database setup, or configuration.

nodes.label: Validation and Safety
nodes.rationale: Provider output remains untrusted; deterministic normalization, skip rules, shared schemas, and backend-owned exports define the accepted result.

nodes.label: Explicit Import Confirmation
nodes.rationale: The file is previewed locally and backend or AI processing must not begin until the user explicitly confirms the import.

nodes.label: In-Memory Job Store
nodes.rationale: Persistence is deliberately omitted for a simple reviewer demo, accepting restart loss and single-instance deployment.

nodes.label: Single-Screen Workflow
nodes.rationale: Upload, preview, progress, results, retry, and export remain on one page to keep the demo fast and preserve context.

nodes.label: Failed Batch Retry
nodes.source_location: Core User Journey 3: Retry Failed Batches

nodes.label: Evidence-First Interface
nodes.rationale: The visual hierarchy foregrounds source rows, mappings, warnings, confidence, and progress rather than decorative analytics.

nodes.label: Backend Validation Rules
nodes.rationale: Final contact selection, enum allowlists, date parsing, skip behavior, and CSV safety are deterministic backend responsibilities.

nodes.label: Contract-First Implementation Sequence
nodes.rationale: Shared schemas and constants are established before backend and frontend features to prevent contract drift.

nodes.label: AI Trust Boundary
nodes.source_location: Local Preview Boundary through Zod Validation
nodes.rationale: Deterministic evidence is computed first, the LLM performs constrained mapping, and backend normalization plus Zod validation decides what is accepted.

nodes.label: Production Migration Path
nodes.rationale: Authenticated ownership and Postgres should precede an idempotent durable queue, observability, provider controls, retention, and AI evaluations.

nodes.label: Retry Idempotency Risk
nodes.source_location: Code quality review > Weak or risky parts

nodes.label: Locked Scope
nodes.rationale: The project remains a no-login reviewer demo and excludes persistence, admin, billing, teams, and other SaaS expansion.

nodes.label: Preview First, Process Second
nodes.rationale: Source data stays in the browser for review; backend validation and AI extraction begin only after explicit confirmation.

nodes.label: Nearly Blank Contact Skip Rationale
nodes.rationale: Row 21 is skipped because it is nearly blank and contains no contact information.
